question.text: In the SEBI vs Raima Equities case, what was found regarding the broker's STR handling?

answer.text: STRs received from the depository were closed by the Principal Officer without stipulating any reason in writing
STRs were filed promptly within 7 days as required
STRs were forwarded to SEBI instead of FIU-IND
No STRs were ever received by the broker

explanation.text: The Logic: Raima Equities had multiple AML failures: (1) arbitrary client risk classification with no documented basis, (2) no AML-specific transaction monitoring system (only stock market risk management), (3) STRs from depository were closed by the Principal Officer WITHOUT stipulating any reason in writing, and (4) no system to identify PEPs. A Rs. 2 lakh penalty was imposed. The Trap: The STRs were not handled properly -- they were received but closed without documentation. This is a critical process failure. STRs must be analyzed and either escalated to FIU-IND or closed with documented reasons.
